subject: Post-call: Multilingual model evals / next steps (EU + APAC)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Anna Müller <anna.mueller@globex-retail.de>, Kenji Sato <ksato@aurelia.jp>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 9 May 2027 14:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: Multilingual model evals / next steps (EU + APAC)

Hi Anna, Kenji —

Thanks again for taking time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side: 

Recap:
- Goal: Verify Redwood's inference quality across EU languages (DE, FR, NL) and APAC locales (JA, KO, ZH) for your customer-facing chat flows and localized product FAQs.
- Key success metrics you called out: answer accuracy on localized intents, hallucination rate < 3% on regulatory/legal prompts, latency under 300ms p50 for short Q/A.
- Current data: you shared ~2k exemplar prompts per locale and flagged two problematic templates for legal content.

Proposed next steps:
1) Redwood will run a 2-week evaluation using our recommended model variants (see below) on your prompt set.
2) We'll provide per-locale perf/quality dashboards, a regression checklist, and example prompt-set mapping for fallbacks.
3) If results meet your thresholds, propose a 90-day POC on Dedicated capacity with per-tenant caching and locale routing.

Recommended models to start with (based on today's discussion):
- en/eu-friendly: rw-instruct-large-quant (conservative responses, lower token cost)
- high-quality multilingual: rw-multi-xl (strong cross-lingual generalization)
- APAC/localized: rw-multi-asia-mid (optimized for JA/KO/ZH tokenization)

I'll attach the eval plan and initial prompt mapping. Can you confirm access to the exemplar prompt set (Drive link) and share any NDA/invoice contact for procurement?

Thanks — I’ll kick off the eval as soon as we have access.

Best,
Marissa
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

Attachment: multilingual-eval-report-v1.pdf (summary plan)
Attachment: prompt-sets-eu-apac.csv (requested mapping)

Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 09:37:00 +0200
Subject: Re: Post-call: Multilingual model evals / next steps (EU + APAC)

Hi Marissa —

Thanks for the clear recap. Confirmed — we gave you Drive access (shared link in-thread) to the EU + APAC prompt bundles. A couple of clarifications before you start:

- For DE legal templates, please prioritize conservative completions and mark any generation that includes legal recommendations as a fail for now.
- For JA/KR product FAQ, we care more about phrasing/naturalness than literal translation.
- Procurement: cc'd our procurement contact is out this week; Kenji will coordinate PO details and send the billing contact.

If you can include a quick benchmark of our current vendor baseline (we'll share sample outputs), that would help quantify uplift.

Best,
Anna
Senior Product Manager, Localization | Globex Retail
anna.mueller@globex-retail.de

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Anna Müller <anna.mueller@globex-retail.de>, Kenji Sato <ksato@aurelia.jp>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 11 May 2027 08:14:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: Multilingual model evals / next steps (EU + APAC)

Thanks Anna — helpful notes. Next update with preliminary results scheduled for EOD Friday. Quick note on the evaluation plan and where we'll focus quality checks: 

Evaluation checklist (high level):
- Per-locale accuracy vs labeled ground truth (micro-F1 for intent mapping)
- Safety/regulatory checks: identify outputs with legal prescriptive language; flag as fail.
- Hallucination detection: we run knowledge-check prompts and mark unsupported assertions.
- Fluency/naturalness: human-rated samples (3 native speakers per locale, blind).
- Latency/throughput: p50/p95 token latency on representative sessions.

Recommended model variants:
- rw-multi-xl (primary) — balanced quality/cost; strong cross-lingual transfer on FR/DE/EN.
- rw-instruct-large-quant (fallback) — cheaper, lower hallucination on concise prompts.
- rw-multi-asia-mid + locale-specific tokenizer tweaks for JA/KO/ZH (to be tested).

Benchmarks & links:
- Eval dashboard: https://redwood-internal.run/evals/DEAL-GLOBEX-2027
- Prompt set (read-only): https://drive.redwood.com/shared/multilingual-prompt-sets

Attached is the initial evaluation report and the prompt map CSV. Please send the vendor baseline outputs when available — we'll run side-by-side scoring.

Action items and owners:
- Marissa: kick off eval run (start Tue EOD) and share dashboard link — in progress.
- Neha: set up human raters for DE/FR/JA (ETA Wed) — @neha_kapoor.
- Rishi: validate latency runbook for Dedicated capacity (ETA Thu) — @rishi_malhotra.
- Kenji: share procurement/billing contact — Kenji.

Thanks — will be in touch with an early results snapshot Friday.

Best,
Marissa

Attachments: multilingual-eval-report-v1.pdf, prompt-sets-eu-apac.csv

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 11 May 2027 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: Multilingual model evals / next steps (EU + APAC)

Quick internal note —

I started the latency baseline run against rw-multi-xl on a dev Dedicated pool with sequence len 128 and batching disabled to simulate low-latency interactive traffic. Early numbers (very preliminary): p50 ~ 220ms, p95 ~ 510ms in our us-west region using A100-rtx equivalent hardware. We'll re-run with locale tokenizers (JA/KO/ZH) and report corrected p95. Also adding KV cache warmup tests for sessionized chat flows.

Neha — I'll need the list of native raters to schedule the blind evaluation.

Rishi
Senior Performance Engineer | Redwood Inference
